title: Solid, Liquid, Gas
objective: After this level you can explain the three everyday states of matter.
summary: Solids keep their shape, liquids flow but keep their volume, and gases fill their container. The difference comes from how tightly packed and how free the particles are.

cards.headline: Pour juice into a glass and it changes shape. It doesn't change amount.
cards.body: Try that with a brick and nothing happens. Let the air out of a balloon and it spreads through the whole room. Three kinds of matter, three very different behaviors. Why?

items.label: Liquid
points: Flows and takes the shape of its container

items.label: Gas
points: Takes the shape of its container
Spreads to fill its whole volume too

cards.headline: It's all in the particles
cards.body: All matter is made of tiny particles: atoms, often joined into molecules. In a solid, the particles are packed tight, often in a neat pattern, and just vibrate in place. In a liquid, they stay close together but slide past each other. In a gas, they are far apart and move on their own, meeting only when they collide. Same particles, different freedom.

cards.headline: Picture a crowd (an analogy)
cards.body: A solid is like a stadium crowd in their seats: packed in, jiggling, going nowhere. A liquid is like a busy dance floor: everyone touching, everyone moving past each other, so the crowd takes the shape of the room. A gas is like a few kids let loose in a huge park, far apart, bumping into each other now and then. Seats keep their shape. Dancers don't.
cards.callout: Analogy: seats = solid, dance floor = liquid, open park = gas

mascot.line: I'm a dance-floor particle myself. Always moving, never leaving the party.

cards.headline: States: sorted
learned: Particles: packed, sliding, or far apart and free

questions.prompt: Which state of matter keeps its own volume but takes the shape of its container?

options.label: Solid
options.rationale: A solid keeps its own shape as well.

options.label: Gas
options.rationale: A gas takes the container's volume too, not just its shape.

questions.explanation: A liquid flows into the shape of its container, but its volume stays the same.

questions.prompt: Why can a liquid flow when a solid can't?

options.label: Its particles are far apart and rarely touch
Its particles are locked in fixed places
Its particles stay close but slide past each other
It has no particles at all
options.rationale: All matter is made of particles.

questions.explanation: Liquid particles stay in contact but can move past each other, so the liquid can flow and take any shape.

questions.prompt: Level 2 said a gas is matter because it takes up space. What does a gas do with the space inside a closed container?

options.label: Spreads to fill all of it
Sinks to the bottom like a liquid
options.rationale: A gas fills the container's whole volume.

options.label: Keeps a fixed shape of its own
Takes up no space at all
options.rationale: Then a balloon would never inflate.

questions.explanation: A gas takes both the shape and the volume of its container, filling every corner.
